nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field and let $v \ne w$ be two distinct points of the projective plane $\mathbb{P}(K^3)$. Call two points orthogonal when the dot product of representative vectors in $K^3$ vanishes, and let $v \times w$ be the point spanned by the cross product of representatives of $v$ and $w$, which is nonzero since $v \ne w$. Then a point $p$ equals $v \times w$ if and only if $p$ is orthogonal to both $v$ and $w$.…
nodes.title: Two distinct lines meet in their cross product

nodes.title: Harbourne constant of a line arrangement

nodes.summary: A line arrangement in the projective plane over a field $K$ is a finite set of at least two lines, each line recorded by its coordinate vector, a point of the dual projective plane $\mathbb{P}(K^3)$.
nodes.title: Line arrangement

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a line arrangement in the projective plane over a field. A point $p$ is a singular point of $A$ if and only if there are two distinct lines of $A$ that both pass through $p$.
nodes.title: Singular points lie on two distinct lines

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a line arrangement in the projective plane over a field. A point $p$ is a singular point of $A$ if and only if its multiplicity $m_p$ in $A$, the number of lines of $A$ through $p$, satisfies $m_p \ge 2$.
nodes.title: Singular points are the points of multiplicity at least two

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be an arrangement of $d$ lines in the projective plane over a field. Every point $p$ has multiplicity $m_p \le d$ in $A$.
nodes.title: Multiplicity is at most the number of lines

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a line arrangement in the projective plane over a field. The multiplicity $m_p$ of a point $p$ in $A$ is the number of lines of $A$ through $p$, that is, of lines of $A$ whose coordinate vector has zero dot product with a representative of $p$.
nodes.title: Multiplicity of a point in a line arrangement

nodes.summary: Every line arrangement in the projective plane over a field has at least one singular point, since any two of its distinct lines meet.
nodes.title: Every line arrangement has a singular point

nodes.summary: The singular points of a line arrangement $A$ in the projective plane over a field form the finite set of intersection points of pairs of distinct lines of $A$, where two distinct lines with coordinate vectors $\ell$ and $\ell'$ meet in the point spanned by the cross product $\ell \times \ell'$ of their representatives.
nodes.title: Singular points of a line arrangement
